#+TITLE: 01 geo.index.doris.align.ES.interface
#+STARTUP: overview

* Dev process setup
  Before executing ANY work item in this plan, open and obey
  the rules defined in this project's per-repo instructions:

    - AGENTS.md  (apache/doris root; also be/src/storage/index/inverted/AGENTS.md, gensrc/AGENTS.md)

  Read the current rules there and follow them.  This plan intentionally does
  not restate any rule -- the per-repo instructions are the single source of truth.
  Doris' own dev skills: doris-skills/skills/develop-with-evidence/SKILL.md
  (=git submodule update --init -- doris-skills= when a work item first needs it).

  Plan-doc language rule (owner, 2026-11-19T11:59Z, translated): every plan doc and fix.archive note in this
  repo is written entirely in English -- no Chinese mixed in.  Chinese user quotes are recorded translated,
  marked "(translated from Chinese)".

  GUIDING PRINCIPLE (owner, 11:53Z message later paragraphs, relayed 12:21Z room doris 20261119T122127Z-c89e64):
  Doris must get a geospatial index on par with ES -- autonomous-driving companies depend on it.  Use the
  FASTEST, most efficient algorithm and the most efficient language; do not let platform / dependency overhead
  drive the design.  Every Frontier choice and work item is judged against this first.

  Repo (owner, same relay): GitHub, not ADO.  origin = the owner's GitHub fork of apache/doris, upstream =
  apache/doris; branch =geo-index= is pushed to the fork; the work will be open-sourced.  Never push to apache/doris.

* Execution environment
  This plan runs on a multi-machine environment described in:

    - ${FLEET_HOME:-$HOME/.fleet}/cluster.md

  Read it before executing.  Where it defines parallelism, it
  outranks subagent fan-out.  This plan does not restate it.

* USER VERBATIM 2026-11-19T11:53Z (Feishu group oc_08aa.., owner; translated from Chinese)
  - "Doris is implemented in Rust; implement a geospatial index in C or Rust and add it to Doris as a plugin or
     addon.  Pick a machine, e.g. c05, clone the doris repo to workspace, create .github/REPL/fix.archive,
     /org_plan 01.geo.index.doris.align.ES.interface.org.txt, and also create a new CLI session doris_geo_index and
     a room doris in tmux.  /kiss! /frontier.  Report after the dev environment is set up."
  - (same message, later paragraphs; Feishu screenshot re-sent via WeChat 12:07Z, relayed to room doris 12:21Z)
    "We need Doris to support a geospatial index like ES; this matters a lot to autonomous-driving companies.
     Use the fastest, most efficient algorithm and the most efficient language.  Ignore the messy platform and
     dependency overhead.  This guiding principle is very important -- write it into the plan."
    + repo on GitHub, not ADO: fork apache/doris to the owner's GitHub account, origin = that fork, upstream =
      apache, push branch geo-index; "we are going to open-source this".
  - context (same chat, 10:04Z-11:24Z): chaochao asked what ES geo_polygon is, whether it is indexed, and how to make
    the same query fast in Doris.  Answer given: ES = geo_point + BKD; Doris 3.x has no spatial index
    (prefix / inverted / bloom / ngram / zonemap only) -> bbox prefilter + ST_Contains, geohash/H3 sort key.

* MEASURED 2026-11-19T12:05Z (c16_chhk_lark, setup)
  - =cli -r= header: "ASK 0 HITL 3 PERM 0 ERR 1 STALL 28 IDLE 30 DEAD 0 GONE 0|171 live/34 box|feed 0s".
    No live session's WORK names doris / geo; no room named doris existed (=room rooms=).
  - c05 (CPC-bazho-42YC9, odsp): 32 cores (avx2), 94 GB RAM (87 avail), /workspace 507 GB free, docker 29.8.1.
    10 tmux sessions already (c05_*_*, rdp-tunnels, sentinel-odsp-b) -- this plan adds one: =doris_geo_index=.
  - Language facts (GitHub languages API + tree): Doris FE = Java, BE = C++ (C++ ~77.5 MB, Java ~85.8 MB, C 0.35 MB);
    there is no Rust in Doris.  The user's claim "Doris is implemented in Rust" is corrected here: the index is C++ in the BE.
  - =apache/doris= master cloned to =c05:/workspace/doris= (blobless, =dbb9b19391= 2026-11-19).
  - What Doris already has that a geo index can reuse (read in the tree, not guessed):
    - BKD tree: =be/src/storage/index/inverted/snii/bkd/= (bkd_builder, bkd_reader, point_sorter, leaf_codec)
      + =snii_bkd_index_writer/reader/query= -- the numeric inverted index.  ONE dimension per point
      (=bytes_per_dim=, value + doc id), so 2-D lat/lon is not native.
    - Geo functions: =be/src/exprs/function/geo/= (ST_*, WKT/WKB parse, =functions_h3.cpp=: h3_lat_lng_to_cell,
      h3_cell_to_boundary, h3_cell_to_lat_lng) and =contrib/h3= (submodule).
    - FE: =nereids/.../scalar/StContains.java=; FE plugins (=fe_plugins/=) are audit / SQL-converter only -- there is
      no storage-index plugin SPI.  A new index type is in-tree BE code + FE DDL, not a loadable plugin.
  - Build env: =apache/doris:build-env-ldb-toolchain-latest= (Docker Hub, the master toolchain) pulled on c05.

* Goal [0/4]
  - [ ] G1 A spatial index on a lat/lon (or POINT) column in Doris BE, built per segment at load time,
        that answers "point within polygon" by visiting only the leaf blocks the polygon's cells cover.
  - [ ] G2 ES-aligned interface: the ES =geo_polygon= / =geo_shape within= query shape maps 1:1 to Doris SQL
        (one documented table of ES DSL -> Doris SQL, incl. lat/lon order and closed-ring rules).
  - [ ] G3 Correct: on a fixed dataset the indexed query returns exactly the rows =ST_Contains= returns
        with the index disabled (diff = 0), incl. boundary points, antimeridian, empty and NULL.
  - [ ] G4 Fast: on >= 100 M points a city-sized polygon scans <= 5% of rows (Profile =RowsInvertedIndexFiltered=
        or the new counter) and wall time beats the bbox-prefilter baseline by >= 3x.

* Dependencies
  - [X] D1 Doris source on c05: =/workspace/doris= (master =dbb9b19391=).
  - [X] D2 Build toolchain image =apache/doris:build-env-ldb-toolchain-latest= on c05.
  - [ ] D3 Submodules the BE build needs (=contrib/clucene=, =contrib/h3=, ... per =build.sh=) -- initialised by the
        build entry point, not by hand (AGENTS.md "Submodules").
  - [ ] D4 thirdparty prebuilt (=thirdparty/installed=) inside the build-env image, or =build-thirdparty.sh=.

* Frontier (decisions that change the plan -- all CLOSED 2026-11-19, room doris acks to 20261119T120404Z-af9d61)
  - :interrupt_TAKEN_AND_CLOSED: F1 Index shape = (a): a cell-id column (BIGINT) + the existing 1-D numeric
    BKD/inverted index on it; a polygon query = polygon -> covering cell ranges -> index lookup -> exact
    ST_Contains on the candidates only.  Cell encoder = our own geohash / Z-order (Morton) code [SUPERSEDED 13:45Z by S2 cell id: S2 is a Doris
    thirdparty on all three branches, see plan 02 MEASURED], NOT H3: H3 is
    master-only and absent from branch-3.1 / branch-4.1, so it would break F3/F4.

    implementation, then efficiency."  Rule for every later choice: simplest and most compatible first, then
    efficiency (refines the GUIDING PRINCIPLE above).
    Rejected: (b) true 2-D BKD (new on-disk format + gensrc upgrade rule); (c) SQL-rewrite-only bbox prefilter
    (that is the Phase B baseline, not the index).

* Context
  - ES side to align with:
    - =geo_point= field + BKD (Lucene LatLonPoint); =geo_polygon= deprecated since 7.12 -> =geo_shape= query with
      GeoJSON/WKT, =relation: within|intersects|disjoint|contains=; GeoJSON order is [lon, lat].
      https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/query-languages/query-dsl/query-dsl-geo-polygon-query
  - Doris side:
    - index overview (no spatial index in 3.x): https://doris.apache.org/docs/3.x/table-design/index/index-overview
    - spatial functions: https://doris.apache.org/docs/3.x/sql-manual/sql-functions/scalar-functions/spatial-functions/st-contains
    - BE index code: =be/src/storage/index/= (inverted/, zone_map/, bloom_filter/, ann/ -- =ann= is the most
      recent "new index type" and the closest template for registration points).
  - Build/test entry points: =build.sh --be=, =run-be-ut.sh=, =run-fe-ut.sh=, =run-regression-test.sh=.

* TODO Phase C -- the index (shape chosen at F1) [5/7]
  :needs: {"tier":"wsl","box":"c05"}
  :after: B
  - Phase C core (cell encoder, polygon cover, tests, memcheck, Docker) is split out to plan 02
    (link "/workspace/doris/.github/REPL/02.geo.index.core.lib.org.txt" 1).  MEASURED 13:45Z: S2 0.10.0 is a
    Doris thirdparty on master, 4.1 and 3.1 -> the F1 cell encoder is S2 (not an own geohash; KISS rung 5).
    C.1/C.2 are done when plan 02 Phase A + Z.1 are done.
  - MEASURED 18:05Z (fix.archive/01.geo.index.reuse.md): a generated BIGINT cell column + the STOCK numeric
    inverted (BKD) index already writes per-segment BKD trees at load (C.1 = DDL only) and answers
    =cell BETWEEN= with ScanRows == hits (1,001 of 100 k) once =inverted_index_skip_threshold= = 0
    (default 50 bypasses the BKD index: 87,411 rows scanned).  So C.1/C.2 need no new BE index code; the work
    moves to C.3 (planner rewrite + keeping the BKD index from being bypassed).
  - [X] C.1 writer: per segment, cells/points -> index file (reuse snii bkd builder for (a)).  BE unit test.
        :test_tool: =./run-be-ut.sh --run --filter=GeoIndex*= green.
        DONE 18:55Z: no writer code -- =s2_cell= (plan 02 Z.1, f5233693e7, ASAN UT =GeoCellTest*= 3/3) feeds a generated
        BIGINT column; the stock BKD inverted-index writer builds the per-segment tree at load (MEASURED with the
        h3 stand-in: 100 k rows in 195 ms, fix.archive/01.geo.index.reuse.md).
  - [X] C.2 reader + query: polygon -> cell set -> row bitmap; exact ST_Contains on the candidates only.
        :test_tool: BE UT: 3 polygons x 10 k random points, bitmap == brute force.
        Implemented by C.3a (=s2_covers= = the polygon -> row bitmap step); flipped with C.3a.
        DONE 19:20Z: BE UT =S2CoversIndexIsSupersetOfStContains=: 3 polygons x 9,491 fixture points, index bitmap is a
        superset of brute-force ST_Contains and equals the row path (ASAN).
  - [ ] C.3 FE: DDL = generated column =geo_cell BIGINT AS (s2_cell(lat, lon))= + =INDEX idx_cell (geo_cell)
        USING INVERTED= (existing numeric index, no new index type; audit 14:00Z finding 4) + planner pushes
        =ST_Contains(<const polygon>, ST_Point(lon, lat))= to the index.
        :test_tool: =./run-fe-ut.sh --run <GeoIndex test>= green; EXPLAIN shows the index predicate.
        Design 18:55Z (/kiss, MEASURED): the FE has no S2 library and cover() needs one, so the cover cannot run
        in the FE without a new Java dependency.  Split C.3 so it ends at a working index:
  - [X] C.3a BE: =s2_covers(<const polygon WKT/shape>, geo_cell[, level, max_cells])= BOOLEAN, approximate
        index predicate (shape of =is_ip_address_in_range= in =be/src/exprs/function/function_ip.h=):
        =evaluate_inverted_index= decodes the const polygon once (=GeoShape::from_encoded= -> =GeoPolygon::polygon()=),
        calls =geo_index::cover()=, ORs one BKD range query per range (=GREATER_EQUAL= & =LESS_EQUAL=,
        =skip_try = true= so the 50% bypass of fix.archive/01.geo.index.reuse.md cannot fire), returns the union.
        =execute_impl= (row path, used when there is no index) = =cell in ranges= with the same ranges, so the
        predicate is correct with or without the index; the user writes
        =WHERE s2_covers(poly, geo_cell) AND ST_Contains(poly, ST_Point(lon, lat))=.
        :kiss: no FE rewrite yet (users / ES mapping write the AND); no new index type; no FE S2 dependency.
        :test_tool: BE UT (bitmap == brute force on fixtures) + on the B.2 cluster: city polygon ScanRows <= 2x hits,
        result == unindexed ST_Contains.
        DONE 19:20Z: 10 M rows, city: 334,307 rows scanned (1.22x hits, 3.3% of rows), hits == unindexed; warm 75 ms
        vs 222 ms full.  Cold 575 ms -> C.4.  (link "/workspace/doris/.github/REPL/fix.archive/01.geo.index.reuse.md" 1)
        :audit: code-review/gpt-6-astra: 1 MEDIUM (one-sided BKD scans) -> C.4 (fix.archive/02.audit.be-adapter.md r2)
  - [X] C.4 bounded BKD range per cover range (audit finding, measured cold 575-1,816 ms): add a two-bound numeric
        query to the BKD path (=build_bkd_query_bounds= + =BkdReader::range(lower, upper)= already exists in SNII; the
        CLucene BKD path for V1/V2 format) and use it in =s2_covers=.  Shared index code -> own UT + audit.
        :test_tool: BE UT for the bounded query (both readers) + cluster: cold <= 2x warm for the 3 polygons, city warm
        <= 62 ms (beats the planar bbox), hits unchanged.
        MEASURED 19:35Z: with =enable_inverted_index_query_cache=false= every s2_covers run costs the cold time
        (city 513-561 ms, InvertedIndexSearcherSearchTime 370 ms; thin 1.8 s, 1.70 s) -> the one-sided scans are the
        whole cost; with the cache, 61-75 ms.
        Design (/kiss):
        - rung 2 (codebase has it): both BKD readers already evaluate a CLOSED interval internally -- SNII
          =BkdReader::range(lower, upper)= and the CLucene =InvertedIndexVisitor= (=query_min= / =query_max=; a one-sided
          query just pins the other side to the type min/max in =construct_bkd_query_value=).  So a bounded range =
          a new query type that fills BOTH bounds; no new index format, no new traversal.
        - New =InvertedIndexQueryType::BETWEEN_QUERY= (closed [lo, hi]); value = a Field TYPE_ARRAY of {lo, hi}.
          Wire it in: =build_bkd_query_bounds= (SNII), =construct_bkd_query_value= + =invoke_bkd_query= /
          =invoke_bkd_try_query= (CLucene; matches() of the generic template already handles min < v < max), the
          query-cache key (encode both bounds), =query_type_to_string=.  =s2_covers= issues one BETWEEN per range.
        - Port note (F3/F4): CLucene BKD exists on 4.1 and 3.1 (=be/src/olap/rowset/segment_v2/inverted_index_reader.cpp=
          on 3.1, same visitor), SNII is master-only.  The CLucene half is what Z.4/Z.5 carry.
        DONE 20:20Z: ASAN UT 50/50 (new SNII + CLucene BETWEEN tests, all existing BKD tests).  Cluster, index query cache
        OFF: cold city 575 -> 105 ms, thin 1,816 -> 109, concave 1,053 -> 148 (cold <= 1.6x warm: PASS); hits unchanged;
        index search 370 -> 3 ms.  city warm 69 ms vs bbox 62 ms: NOT yet met -> C.5.
        :audit: code-review/gpt-6-astra r3: 0 findings (fix.archive/02.audit.be-adapter.md)
  - [X] C.5 cache the parsed polygon + cover ranges per FunctionContext in =s2_covers= (row path) the way
        =StRelationState= does for ST_Contains, so a constant polygon is parsed and covered once per fragment.
        :test_tool: cluster city warm <= 62 ms (beats the planar bbox of B.3), hits unchanged; GeoCellTest green.
        :SUPERSEDED_BY_MEASUREMENT: 20:30Z, no code: back-to-back 10-run medians with profile off give city
        51 ms (bar 62 ms, bbox 57 ms and wrong), thin 56 ms, concave 97 ms; s2_covers alone 49 ms vs 56 ms with the
        recheck -> polygon parsing is not the bottleneck; the "69 ms" was profile overhead.  R-KISS: no cache.
        (fix.archive/01.geo.index.reuse.md section 5)
  - [ ] C.3b FE: Nereids rule rewrites =ST_Contains(<const polygon>, ST_Point(lon, lat))= on a table whose
        =geo_cell= is =s2_cell(lat, lon)= into =s2_covers(poly, geo_cell) AND ST_Contains(...)=.  Pure FE pattern
        match, no S2 in the FE.
        :test_tool: =./run-fe-ut.sh --run <GeoIndex rule test>= green; EXPLAIN shows =s2_covers=.
